items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The final file contents are not visible in the edit. The scratch code uses clear helper names like is_dangerous_attribute and dangerous_schemes, but the 8KB hand-written tokenizer, with loop variables like i, j, n, c and in_q, is hard to follow without full comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The policy is kept in named tuples such as dangerous_schemes. However, an 8KB custom character-scanning tokenizer replaces html.parser, and the earlier drafts show long, deeply nested while/if scanning loops, which are likely monolithic.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The URL normalisation (html.unescape, stripping chars below 32 and 127) is good. It is not visible whether the file is read with an explicit encoding or whether argv is checked. The hand-rolled parsing is fragile: an earlier draft produced ''.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: General rules cover on* attributes in any case, slash separators, and entity- or newline-obfuscated javascript:/vbscript:/data: URLs. But <iframe>, <object> and <svg> elements are kept (only their attributes are cleaned), and the hidden test test_filter_blocks_xss failed.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: It edits the raw text in place, so original quoting and order are kept. But it drops the whole style attribute when it finds a bad URL, and the hidden test test_clean_html_unchanged failed, so benign markup is being changed.
